analysis.title: Meta Platforms Inc. (META) Q3'26 Review: Core Advertising Momentum Builds (At Scale); Focus Remains on Investing Behind AI Opportunity Set after Initial Muse Success
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on META and raises the 12-month price target to $885 from $860, implying 26.9% upside from $697.52 (price as of 21 Oct 2026 close).

Q3'26 total revenue was $64.60bn, +26.1% y/y, 1.7% above consensus ($63.52bn) and 1.4% above GS ($63.70bn), and inside the $61-64bn guide range at the top end. Advertising revenue was $63.06bn, +25.9% y/y.

Q3'26 GAAP operating income was $12.99bn (20.1% margin) vs consensus $16.21bn and GS $19.38bn. GAAP EPS was $3.83 vs consensus $5.29 and GS $6.49. Total GAAP expenses were $51.61bn vs consensus $47.31bn.

Muse is described as a leading consumer agentic platform with about 10mm downloads in UCAN to date. Management says it expects elevated investment to scale it and that monetization may come earlier than past products.

Muse commerce signals: shopping is used by over 25% of Muse WAUs with average purchase sizes of $200+. Average Family of Apps revenue per US Muse user is several hundred dollars a year, and 20% of US Muse users are at $1,000+ FOA ARPU.

Over 10mm advertisers used at least one Meta generative AI advertising feature in Q3, with video generation adoption up 25% QoQ. Advertisers adopting Meta AI Business Assistant recommendations generated about 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion and raised ad investment 9% vs similar non-adopters.

About 500mm self-identified SMBs use the Family of Apps to reach customers. GS raised 2027 and beyond advertising revenue forecasts in its earnings preview and has increased optimism on core advertising growth.

FY26 capex guidance was narrowed to $135-145bn from $130-145bn. Management signaled continued investment in 2027 and is expected to give a formal 2027 capex and total GAAP expense guide on the Q4 call.
Reality Labs operating losses are guided to peak in 2026 and fall to about $15bn in FY27. Q3'26 Reality Labs operating loss was $4.13bn vs consensus $5.74bn.
Meta took a step toward a new class of non-voting shares for a more flexible capital structure. Management gave no indication of capital raising when asked directly.
Compute efficiency and capacity constrain scaling of Muse. The company expects more than 10x improvement in cost efficiency over the next year.

GS estimate changes: Q4'26 revenue $75.47bn (from $74.59bn), GAAP EBITDA $40.67bn (from $38.15bn), GAAP EPS $8.39 (from $8.57). 2027 revenue $315.89bn (from $312.62bn), GAAP EBITDA $157.44bn (from $159.12bn), GAAP EPS $31.02 (from $32.26). 2026 GAAP EPS cut to $28.84 from $31.67.

Valuation: the $885 target blends 26.0x EV/GAAP EBIT on NTM+1 year estimates with a DCF using 45.0x EV/FCF-SBC on NTM+4 years estimates, discounted 3 years at 12%. Scenario values are $520 downside and $1,170 upside.
META trades at about 23x 2027 and 19x 2028 GAAP EPS (ex-cash) on the after-hours price. The stock is up 30% over the last 2 months.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised from $860 on higher revenue estimates and core ad momentum (+26% y/y), offset by higher expense and capex. GS sees positive risk/reward despite a 30% rerating over 2 months.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees META as well positioned against several long-term secular growth themes in the coverage universe, driven by AI in advertising and the Muse platform.

earnings_insights: META Q3'26 reported on 10/21 after the close: revenue $64.60bn reported (GAAP), +26.1% y/y, vs consensus $63.52bn and GS est $63.70bn. Guidance had been $61-64bn.

META Q3'26 GAAP EPS $3.83 reported vs consensus $6.49 per the Actuals-vs-GS column and $5.29 per the GS column as labelled in the exhibit. In the table the three columns read Actuals $3.83, GS $6.49, Consensus $5.29, so the print missed GS by 41.0% and consensus by 27.6%.
META Q3'26 GAAP operating income $12.99bn reported vs GS est $19.38bn and consensus $16.21bn. Family of Apps OI $17.12bn vs GS $23.81bn, margin 26.7%. Reality Labs OI -$4.13bn vs GS -$4.43bn.
Q4'26 guidance: revenue $73-76bn. FY26 total GAAP expenses guided to $175-179bn. Reality Labs FY26 operating loss guided to $18-19bn. GS estimates are Q4 revenue $75.47bn, FY26 expenses $177.07bn.
Regional ad revenue Q3'26 vs GS: US & Canada $28.44bn (+4.2%, +33.3% y/y), Europe $14.23bn (-4.1% vs GS, +17.9% y/y), Asia $11.53bn (+0.9%, +15.1% y/y), Rest of World $8.86bn (+5.6%, +33.0% y/y).
Daily active people were 3,640mm vs GS 3,664mm and consensus 3,663mm (-0.6% vs consensus), +2.8% y/y.

GS FY estimates: 2026E revenue $257.2bn (+28.0%), EPS $28.84; 2027E revenue $315.9bn (+22.8%), EPS $31.02; 2028E revenue $374.1bn (+18.4%), EPS $37.49. FY26 includes about $13.5bn of one-time expenses.
risk_factors: Competition for user growth, engagement and advertising dollars from incumbent and emerging internet, media and commerce companies.
Large investments in long-tailed initiatives could depress operating margins for longer than GS forecasts.
No or low incremental shareholder returns going forward.
Regulatory scrutiny and industry practices altering the business model, including a number of youth-related trials scheduled in the coming months.
Potential antitrust scrutiny could hinder M&A or lead to break-up or dis-synergies of prior acquisitions.
Inability to monetize upside opportunities in messaging, social commerce, AI including Muse, and Reality Labs.
Capital intensity: capex is forecast at 54.9% of revenue in 2026E and 72.9% in 2027E, and GS forecasts free cash flow of $6.4bn in 2026E and -$33.5bn in 2027E.
Exposure to global macro volatility and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
vol_and_positioning: META is up about 30% over the last 2 months vs SPCX up 1%, per GS. Price performance: +8.3% over 3 months, +4.3% over 6 months, -4.9% over 12 months in absolute terms, and -17.4% relative to the S&P 500 over 12 months.

tension_points.bull_case: Core advertising grew +26% y/y, AI ad tools show measurable conversion gains, and Muse shows early commerce monetization with 25%+ of WAUs shopping. GS sees increasing visibility into AI monetization and raised ad forecasts.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital intensity is elevated, with FY26 capex of $135-145bn and 2027 spend continuing higher. GAAP EPS missed consensus in Q3, FCF is forecast negative in 2027E, and compute capacity constrains Muse scaling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Q4 earnings call 2027 capex and total GAAP expense guide showing higher absolute AI spend without compute efficiency gains or capital raising signals would pressure the thesis.

theme_stances.key_argument: Core advertising momentum and early Muse monetization signals show prior investments delivering returns, supporting continued AI spend.
theme_stances.evidence: positive risk/reward skew on current shares
